CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH RAI K  ORAL/CAV JUDGMENT

This appeal is directed against the judgment of conviction dated 24.01.2022 and order of sentence dated 25.01.2022 passed in Special Case (POCSO) No.22/2028 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge & FTSC-I (POCSO) at Vijayapura (hereinafter referred to as 'learned Special Judge'), whereby the learned Special Judge convicted the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 36 and 344 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for period of two years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month for the offence punishable under Section 366 of IPC.

sentences.text: Further, he is sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of twoyears and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month for the offence punishable under Section 344 of IPC.
It is also directed that both the sentences including non-payment of fine shall run concurrently.

sentences.text: The abridged facts of the prosecution case are that,
PW4 -victim and the appellant-accused belongs to Angadageri Village.
The appellant went to Goa to eke out his livelihood and he used to visit his village occasionally.
During such time, he was well acquainted with victim-PW4 and he expressed his love to her and also intends to marry her.

Accordingly, on 03.09.2017 at about 01:30 p.m., the appellant took the victim- PW4 from the lawful custody of her parents-PWs.1 and 5 from Angadageri village to Bewandi near Pune and stayed together for a period of 23 days.

In the meanwhile, on 06.09.2017 the father of victim-PW1 lodged a complaint before the respondent- Police about missing of his daughter specifically against accused Nos.1 to 6 alleging that accused No.1 has kidnapped his daughter at the instance of accused Nos.2 to 6 as per Ex.P1.
 3.

On the strength of Ex.P1, the respondent-Police registered the case in Crime No.179/2017 against the appellant and others for the offences punishable under Sections 363 and 109 r/w Section 149 of IPC as per Ex.P44.
Subsequently, PW.4- victim and accused were traced on 26.09.2017 at Zari Area near Airport Road at Goa.

Thereafter, the respondent-Police  -4-  NC: 2026:KHC-K:708 Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35335136/
3  CRL.A No. 200028 of 2022 HC-KAR recorded the statement of the victim and implicated accused No.1 and others in the alleged crime.

sentences.text:
After conducting investigation, the respondent-Police laid charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 363,
376 and 109 r/w Section 149 of IPC and Section 5(l) r/w Sections 6 and 17 of POCSO Act.

4. To prove the charges leveled against the accused,
the prosecution in total examined 20 witnesses as PWs.1 to 20 and marked 46 documents as Exs.P1 to P46.
The accused neither examined any witness on his behalf nor marked any documents.

5. After assessment of oral and documentary evidence, the learned Special Judge convicted the accused No.1-appellant for the offences punishable under Sections 366 and 344 of IPC and sentenced him as stated supra.
The said judgment is challenged in this appeal.
6. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State.

-5-  NC: 2026:KHC-K:708  CRL.A No. 200028 of 2022 HC-KAR Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35335136/
4  7.

entities.text: HC-KAR Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from urging several contentions, learned counsel for the appellant primarily contented that the judgment under this appeal suffers from perversity and illegality, since the learned Special Judge has failed to appreciate the evidence in a right perspective.
He contented that, none of the prosecution witnesses supported the case of prosecution including the victim, who was examined as PW4.
In such circumstances, the learned Special Judge convicted the accused based on surmises and conjectures.
He also contended that the victim specifically denied her statements under 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
Nevertheless, the prosecution also failed to prove the age of the victim that she was minor at the time of incident.
In such circumstance, the judgment of the Trial Court is not sustainable both under law and on facts.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the appeal.

8. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader contended that the leaned Sessions Judge after meticulously examining the evidence on record, convicted the accused in a well reasonable judgment, which does not call for any interference.

He contended that, in the 164 statement of the victim, she categorically stated that she had love affair with  -6-  NC: 2026:KHC-K:708  CRL.A No. 200028 of 2022 HC-KAR Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35335136/
5 accused No.1 and knowing fully that she was minor at the time of incident, accused No.1 taken her to Bewandi near Pune and from there to Goa and had sexual intercourse on her.

entities.text: Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, the learned Special Judge has rightly convicted accused for the offences punishable under Sections 366 and 344 of IPC.
Though, victim and other witnesses have not supported the case of prosecution, the Court can convict the accused, since the victim was minor at the time of incident.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the appeal.
 9.

Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and on perusal of the impugned judgment so also the material available on record, the sole point that would arise for my consideration is:
 "Whether the judgment under this appeal  suffers from perversity or illegality and the same  requires any interference by this Court?"
 10.
On careful perusal of the evidence and the documents placed before this Court, it is not dispute that the victim and accused No.1 belongs to the same village.

As per the complaint averments at Ex.P1, it is stated by PW.1-the  -7-  NC: 2026:KHC-K:708  CRL.A No. 200028 of 2022 HC-KAR Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35335136/
6 father of victim that accused No.1 along with others kidnapped his daughter.

entities.text: HC-KAR Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, during the course of evidence, PW.1 totally given a go bye to the complaint averments and denied the same.

Though, PW.1 was cross examined at length by the prosecution, nothing worthwhile has been elicited from him to rely his complaint at Ex.P1.
 11.

Nevertheless, though the prosecution examined victim-PW4, wherein she has also specifically denied the incident and stated that neither she accompanied accused No.1 as stated in the complaint nor the accused forced her to accompany him to Bewandi near Pune or Goa on the guise of marrying her.
She also stated that at the time of incident, she had been to her uncle's house and stayed there for the reason that her parents were forcibly insisting her to get marry.
The victim has also specifically denied the same in her 164 statement.
Additionally, PW5-the mother of victim also turned hostile to the case of prosecution.
In such circumstances, the prosecution has failed to prove the charges leveled against accused for the offences punishable under Sections 366 or 344 of IPC.
There are no such evidence available on record, except the evidence of Investigating Officer and the other official  -8-  NC: 2026:KHC-K:708  CRL.A No. 200028 of 2022  HC-KAR witnesses.

No doubt, the prosecution has placed the birth Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35335136/
7 certificate of victim as per Ex.P34 which depicts that the victim was aged above 17 years.

entities.text: Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, when the very incident itself is denied by the victim, complainant and the mother of victim, much credence cannot be attached to the age proof of victim, when the evidence lacks to connect accused No.1 in the alleged incident/crime.

12. It is settled position of law that the evidence of official witnesses cannot be discarded only for the reason that they are the official witnesses, but in the same time, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pradeep Narayana Madgaonkar and others vs. State of Maharastra reported in (1995) 4 SCC 255 held

entities.text: Pradeep Narayana Madgaonkar and others vs. State of Maharastra reported in (1995) 4 SCC 255
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that, the testimony of the official witness cannot be discarded solely on the basis that they are the official, but in the same time, without there being any corroboration, the evidence of the official witness cannot be acted upon.
The Court has to look into corroborative piece of evidence of official witness, since there is a possibility of false implication.

13. Further, to prove the charge leveled under Section 366 of IPC, the ingredients of the offence has to be proved i.e.,
 -9-  NC: 2026:KHC-K:708  CRL.A No. 200028 of 2022 HC-KAR accused must kidnap the victim from the lawful guardian against her will, by compelling her to marry.

In the instant Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35335136/
8 case, the victim herself has stated that the accused at no point of time had forced her to accompany him or insisted her to marry him.

entities.text: Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, the ingredients of Section 366 of IPC does not attracts in this case.

14. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mousam Singha Roy v. State of W.B. reported in (2003) 12 SCC 377 has made an observation in respect of moral conviction that,
wandering on strong suspicion is not an option to decide a case by the Sessions Court and held in paragraph No.27 as under:
 "27.

entities.text: Mousam Singha Roy v. State of W.B. reported in (2003) 12 SCC 377
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before we conclude, we must place on  record the fact that we are not unaware of the  degree of agony and frustration that may be  caused to the society in general and the families of  the victims in particular, by the fact that a heinous  crime like this goes unpunished, but then the law  does not permit the courts to punish the accused  on the basis of moral conviction or on suspicion  alone.
The burden of proof in a criminal trial never  shifts, and it is always the burden of the  prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable  doubt on the basis of acceptable evidence.
In a  similar circumstance this Court in the case of  Sarwan Singh Rattan Singh v. State of Punjab.

entities.text: Sarwan Singh Rattan Singh v. State of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is no doubt a matter of regret  that a foul cold-blooded and cruel  murder should go unpunished.
There  - 10 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:708  CRL.A No. 200028 of 2022 HC-KAR  may also be an element of truth in  the prosecution story against the  accused.

Considered as a whole, the  prosecution story may be true; but Parashuram S/O Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35335136/
9  between 'may be true' and 'must be  true' there is inevitably

entities.text: Mallappa Madar vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
a long  distance to travel and the whole of  this distance must be covered by the  prosecution by legal, reliable and  unimpeachable evidence before an  accused can be convicted."
 15.
In the instant case, albeit there is short of evidence to prove the charges leveled against accused No.1, the learned Special Judge convicted accused No.1/appellant based on surmise and conjecture.
In my considered view, the said conviction order cannot be sustained and interference is required in the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.

Accordingly, I answer point raised above in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER (i) The Criminal Appeal is allowed. s (ii) The judgment of conviction dated 24.01.2022 and order of sentence dated 25.01.2022 passed in Special Case (POCSO) No.22/2018 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge & FTSC-I (POCSO) at Vijayapura, is hereby set aside.
- 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:708 HC-KAR (iii) Consequently, the appellant-accused No.1 is acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 366 and 344 of IPC.
(iv) Bail bond of the accused and that of his sureties shall stand cancelled.
(v) The fine amount, if any, deposited by accused No.1 is ordered to be refunded to him on due identification after appeal period is over.
Registry to directed to send back the TCR along with certified copy of this judgment to the concerned Court, forthwith.
